extracted.intended_audience: NIH extramural research community — investigators, grant applicants, institutional administrators, and research administrators preparing or managing NIH grant applications
extracted.subtask_description: Keeping current with NIH extramural policy, application-format, review-process, and resource updates that affect preparing, submitting, and managing NIH grant applications and awards. The page is an NIH news digest linking to specific guidance (e.g., DMS plan format, review-process changes, program announcements).

rubrics_metrics.name: Selecting appropriate research models / NAMs
rubrics_metrics.description: Investigators should select the models most appropriate for their specific research questions even as NIH supports a wide range of scientifically sound approaches and encourages New Approach Methodologies (NAMs).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NIH supports approaches that enhance human relevance and translational potential, but investigators must choose the model(s) that best fit their hypothesis and specific aims. Use NAMs when scientifically appropriate and justified; prioritize human relevance and translational potential when selecting models.

rubrics_metrics.name: Follow PF5 Collaborative International Research Projects application format
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants to the new Collaborative International Research Projects (PF5) should learn key features and the required application format for PF5 awards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Watch NIH’s 6‑minute PF5 overview to understand PF5 key features, required application structure, and administrative details such as how applications may be split into linked awards after review and before Just‑in‑Time requests. Ensure PF5 applications conform to the specified format and consider the possibility of award splitting when planning project structure and budgets.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use the 2026 Pilot Data Management and Sharing (DMS) Plan format
rubrics_metrics.description: NIH issued a 2026 Pilot DMS Plan format based on a simplified set of required elements to use when preparing Data Management and Sharing Plans.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When preparing a DMS Plan for applicable applications, use the 2026 Pilot format and include the simplified required elements specified in that format. Consult the linked resources for exact element requirements and examples to ensure compliance with NIH expectations for data management and sharing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Embed replication and reproducibility in applications and awards
rubrics_metrics.description: NIH encourages embedding replication and reproducibility throughout research, and has launched initiatives (e.g., Gold Standard Science plan, Replication and Reproducibility Initiative) to drive and incentivize these practices across the biomedical enterprise.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Address replication and reproducibility explicitly in application narratives where applicable (methods, design, statistical power, validation plans). Consider including plans to replicate findings, share materials/data, and document methods to increase reliability; review the NIH highlighted topic and guidance for specific expectations and examples.

rubrics_metrics.name: Understand 'Competitive But Not Discussed' scoring implications
rubrics_metrics.description: Following emergency modifications to review processes, the middle third of applications in a study section were designated as 'competitive but not discussed' recognizing that strong applications may fall below a 33% cut off.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be aware that being scored 'competitive but not discussed' means an application fell into a middle tier in review and may not receive panel discussion; understand how this designation affects chances for funding and what administrative or resubmission options exist. Consult the detailed NIH explanation for implications and next steps after receiving that score.

rubrics_metrics.name: Centralized peer review implications
rubrics_metrics.description: NIH centralized all peer review within the Center for Scientific Review (CSR), an organizational change intended to strengthen efficiency, competition, and transparency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should note that peer review is consolidated in CSR; this may affect study section assignments, review timelines, and processes. Review program notices and updates about centralization to understand any changes to submission routing, reviewer expectations, and timing that could affect application preparation and strategy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be aware of program re-openings and eligibility changes (e.g., NIH Seed Fund)
rubrics_metrics.description: Announcements such as 'NIH’s Seed Fund is back in action' signal program-level changes affecting innovators, founders, and small R&D-driven companies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you are a small business or entrepreneur, monitor program re-openings and guidance to determine eligibility, application timing, and any new or reinstated funding mechanisms. Follow the linked program pages for specific eligibility criteria, application formats, and deadlines.
